subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@fastretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency & throughput follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned:

What I heard:
- Primary goal: integrate LLM-based product search reranking into checkout flows with sub-100ms UI latency targets (goal: p95 < 50ms, p99 < 120ms).
- Typical request size: ~12-20 tokens generated per query, average request payload ~1-2 KB.
- Traffic profile: steady baseline ~200 req/min with 10% hourly spikes up to ~1,000 req/min during peak campaigns.
- Data constraints: no customer PII persisted in the hosted service (they prefer redaction), but log-level telemetry is acceptable for debugging.

Initial qualification & recommendation:
- Hosted API would be a fast way to pilot (quick signup, managed capacity, and streaming responses) and is likely to meet average latency needs for small scale pilots.
- Given your p95/p99 requirements and sustained peak throughput (1k req/min), Dedicated capacity is the recommended path for production: reserved GPU pools give predictable tail latency, configurable autoscaling/burst policies, and the ability to pin model versions.
- If the final requirement becomes sub-50ms p99 at peak, we should evaluate private deployment (VPC or on-prem) as an option, but lets confirm with benchmark numbers first.

Proposed next steps:
1) You to confirm: target SLOs (p95/p99), typical token lengths for inference, and acceptable failover behavior.
2) Share a small sample of 200 anonymized queries (redacted) so we can run a focused latency/throughput benchmark.
3) Schedule a 60-minute benchmarking session with infra (Vivek) + product (Rishi) to validate dedicated sizing and autoscale settings.
4) Redwood to provide a short mutual action plan and a two-week dedicated trial quote for verification.

Attachments: fastretail_requirements.pdf (your summary), redwood_latency_benchmarks-2026.pdf (our reference numbers)

If that matches your view, I'll send the MAP and proposed time slots for the benchmarking session.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.co@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198


From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@fastretail.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency & throughput follow-up

Marissa

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Our hard SLO is p95 < 30ms for the in-checkout inference call; p99 goal is 80ms but we can tolerate 120ms only during rare outages.
- Average token length is closer to 16 tokens; however re-ranking requests can occasionally push to 40 tokens for large baskets.
- Peak traffic: last Black Friday we saw sustained 800-1,200 req/min for ~2 hours.

Given the p95 target (30ms) and sustained peaks, it sounds like Dedicated capacity is the right direction. We're open to a staged approach (hosted pilot for feature dev, then dedicated for production).

Two asks before we schedule the benchmark:
1) Can Redwood run benchmarks using our sample dataset but emulate our peak traffic profile?
2) What's the typical lead time and commitment for Dedicated reserved capacity (and do you offer short trial windows)?

Thanks — I'll get the anonymized sample over by EOD tomorrow.

—Alex
VP Product, FastRetail
alex.johnson@fastretail.com | +1 617-555-0110


From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@fastretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency & throughput follow-up

Alex / Priya

Great — thanks for the details and for sending the sample. Quick answers to your asks:

1) Benchmarking with your sample: yes. We can emulate your peak profile (800-1,200 req/min) and run p95/p99 latency sweeps across our hosted and dedicated configurations. Suggest we run two runs: (A) hosted pilot configuration (best-effort) and (B) dedicated sizing candidate (reserved pool + autoscale rules).

2) Lead time & trial: Dedicated reserved capacity typically requires a minimum 30-day reservation for production contracts, but we offer a two-week evaluation plan (trial capacity) for qualified customers — that's what I propose for FastRetail so we can validate p95/p99 at peak without long-term commitment up front.

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
- Week 0: Sign evaluation NDA + trial order (two-week dedicated trial).
- Week 1: Redwood runs benchmarks (shared results + kernel/config suggestions).
- Week 2: Joint performance tuning (quantization/profiles, batching, KV caching) and final sizing recommendation.
- Post-trial: Decision (hosted for lower ops overhead vs dedicated reserved for production SLA).

I'll send a short MAP and a trial quote (including pricing bands for 30/90/365 commit) by EOD. If you're OK with the trial, can we schedule the benchmark session on Wednesday or Thursday this week? Vivek is available Wed 10-12 and Thu 2-4 PT.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
